name: Where-Object { }
summary: Keeps the objects for which a PowerShell condition is true ($_ is the current object).
action: keeps objects where a condition holds
description: Use this when the simple Where-Object form is not enough: several conditions joined with -and / -or, -not, a regex on a path, or a lookup of another object (for example the parent process). The condition is PowerShell code and is passed as written; Command Lens checks that brackets and quotes balance. ? is the short alias.

params.label: Condition
params.desc: PowerShell condition; $_ is the object being tested. Join conditions with -and / -or; negate with -not.
